10.1002/adfm.201900412.argus: P081 (Han et al. 2019, BNNS aerogel / epoxy), one abstract-only row, 15 vol% -> 6.07 W/(m K), direction unknown

findings.result: Exact agreement at 15 vol% (6.07). Sarikhani et al. digitized 9 more points from Fig. 1(d) (1.3-20 vol%) and state they are parallel to the lamellar layers (in-plane).

The review quotes 6.54 (in-plane) and 0.7 (through-plane) at 15 vol%. In the independent digitization 6.54 is the 20 vol% point and 15 vol% gives 6.07, as in ARGUS (from the abstract), so the review pairs the 20 vol% value with the 15 vol% loading.

10.1002/adfm.201900412.verdict: ARGUS value confirmed by an independent extraction; the review's 6.54 belongs to 20 vol%.
10.1002/adfm.201900412.action: None now. If the full text becomes accessible, set the direction to in-plane and add the Fig. 1(d) series (two secondary sources agree on both).

10.1016/j.compscitech.2020.108304.argus: Wei et al. 2020 (AlN honeycomb / epoxy), 47.26 vol% -> 9.48 (parallel) and 4.45 (perpendicular)

10.3390/polym14142950.argus: Polymers 2022 (AlN, BN and AlN-BN in epoxy), AlN/EP at 30 wt% -> 1.1 and 75 wt% -> 6.83 W/(m K)

findings.result: No common loading. He et al. list this paper's AlN/epoxy series at 10, 20, 40, 50, 60, 70 and 80 wt% (0.47-6.86 W/(m K)). The paper's text gives 75 wt% as the highest AlN loading studied ("AlN/EP 75 wt% ... 6.83 W/(m K)"), and the compiled 80 wt% value (6.86) is within 0.5% of the paper's 75 wt% value.

10.3390/polym14142950.verdict: ARGUS matches the paper's text; the compilation's top loading exceeds the paper's stated maximum.
10.3390/polym14142950.action: None. Not a test row either way (the paper is in ARGUS, so the leakage guard drops it).
